thread.title: Microsoft: This May Be The Best Tech Stock You Can Own Right Now - Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT)

author: Victor Dergunov
title: Microsoft: This May Be The Best Tech Stock You Can Own Right Now - Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT)
text:
Source: TechCrunch.com
Unlike a lot of other high-profile tech companies, Microsoft ( MSFT ) is showing no difficulty keeping up with analyst expectations. Microsoft’s businesses appear extremely stable, and the company’s near monopoly in desktop OS should enable Microsoft to weather an economic downturn far better than most companies.
Microsoft’s stock has performed extremely well in recent years, is up by over 30% in the last 52 weeks alone, and, despite the sharp correction in tech names, is only 6% lower than its all-time high.
MSFT 1-Year Chart
Source: StockCharts.com
With growth fizzling out left and right, ironically, it’s Microsoft whose growth story appears to be alive and well. Due to Microsoft’s stability, its dominant position in various sectors, and relatively strong top and bottom line growth potential, Microsoft’s stock is likely to continue to garner strong demand, and the company’s share price should increase going forward.
Microsoft: A Bright Spot in a Very Cloudy Market From Apple ( AAPL ) to Amazon ( AMZN ) to Facebook ( FB ) to Nvidia ( NVDA ) and to many others, technology companies have been missing revenue estimates and are guiding lower. This implies that many businesses are slowing down substantially, and some are looking at single-digit growth or lower even next year and beyond. This phenomenon is creating a vacuum in the technology space, as fewer high-quality companies with immediate growth prospects remain standing.
Microsoft is clearly one of the few that remains standing:
EPS: $1.14 vs $0.96 estimates, 19% beat, up 36% YoY. Revenues: $29.08 billion vs $27.9 billion estimate, 4.3% beat, 19% YoY increase. Forward guidance: $31.9 billion - $32.7 billion, in line with estimates for $32.25 billion. Commercial cloud revenues: $8.5 billion vs $8.3 billion estimates, up 47% YoY. Azure’s revenue: Up 76% YoY. Personal computing revenues: $10.7 billion vs $10.18 billion estimates, 15% YoY increase. Productivity and business processes: $9.8 billion vs $9.39 billion estimates, up by 19% YoY. Microsoft's Revenues by Year
Source: Statista.com - This year (fiscal 2019) revenues are projected to rise to roughly $125 billion , and next year to about $138 billion.
Microsoft’s numbers indicate that the company is still firing on all cylinders, beating estimates in all its business segments. It's also likely that momentum will continue to be strong with Microsoft due to significant growth in its cloud businesses, its near monopoly in desktop OS, as well as other constructive factors.
Worldwide Marketshare PC Desktop OS
Source: Statista.com - Microsoft remains remarkably dominant with roughly 83% worldwide marketshare.
Momentum Remains Very Strong with Microsoft Microsoft surpassed earnings estimates once again last quarter. But this is nothing new for the company, as Microsoft has beat EPS estimates in every one of its last eight quarters . If we look at the company’s past four quarters, Microsoft has surpassed estimates by an average of about 12%.
EPS History (Past 4 Quarters)
Source: Nasdaq.com
Profitability Continues to Strengthen So, how does Microsoft continuously surpass analysts’ estimates? Microsoft has become an incredibly efficient money-making machine over the years, and with its increasing operations in cloud and in other high-margin areas the company may continue to become increasingly more profitable in future years.
While revenues increased by 19% YoY last quarter's operating income grew by 29% . Additionally, net income increased by 34% and EPS grew by 36%. Microsoft’s profitability capacity is truly impressive, and with fewer companies delivering high growth and increased profitability Microsoft’s stock is likely to continue to garner extremely high demand.
Profitability Highlights
Source: Microsoft 8K
Microsoft: A Valuation Perspective Many company growth prospects are evaporating. For instance, Apple is likely looking at revenue growth of just 4% or 5% in coming years . Nvidia is likely facing a similar problem of low single digit to possibly no growth next year. Facebook and many others are looking at severe margin compression and limited or no profitability growth going forward.
However, Microsoft does not share this problem. In fact, Microsoft’s revenues are expected to increase by double digits this year and next. Moreover, relatively robust revenue growth could continue beyond 2020. Furthermore, EPS is expected to grow by about 15% this year and by 13.2% next year .
Also, it's possible, likely even that due to its propensity for beating analysts’ projections, Microsoft will continue to surpass EPS estimates. If we apply a similar percentage beat rate as the past four quarters (12%), Microsoft could earn about $5.64 in EPS next year (this is still lower than higher end estimates).
$5.64 in EPS implies that Microsoft is currently trading at about 19 times forward earnings. Is this expensive in today’s market? I would argue that for a dominant market leader likely to continue to bring in double-digit top and bottom line growth it isn’t expensive, and Microsoft remains a strong buy today.
The Bottom Line: Microsoft Remains a Strong Buy In a segment littered with slower or “no more” growth stories, Microsoft offers a compelling opportunity. Unlike many other prominent tech names that are facing clear slowdowns and reduced profitability potential, Microsoft continues to fire on all cylinders. Moreover, the company is likely to continue to deliver solid top and bottom line growth going forward in 2019, 2020 and possibly beyond. Therefore, Microsoft will likely continue to outperform most other tech names, as well as the broader market averages, which makes the stock a strong buy right now.
